txt: She mumbles some kind of a response, then hacks something into her handkerchief.
The cleaning lady shrugs and returns to sweeping.
"*We* won't be killing anyone. And *you* shouldn't say things like that. You're a police officer... there's been enough killing. I've *seen* it..." She coughs.
"Addicts, all of them... And sometimes I hear them screaming." She winces.
"Ah!" the cleaning lady says, leaning on her broom. "All I know about politics is that it has brought us more harm than good."
"Ask away, policeman."
"De Ruyters are at the end of this hallway, right next to the communal bathroom."
"Economy? Why should anyone care about economy?!" She shrugs and returns to sweeping.
"Give me a moment..." The cleaning lady still seems to be having difficulty breathing.
"Give me a moment." An elderly woman is leaning on her broom, her knuckles white as bone. She seems to be having difficulty breathing.
"Go ahead then. What do you want to know, policeman?"
"Go check the backyard door, maybe someone there will..." She trails off, leaving the sentence unfinished.
"Good. We've had enough problems with bums and drunks and thieves loitering in the hallway... You have no business here."
"Great. Young people, they're worse than rats, you know -- always littering the hallways with trinkets and empty beer cans..."
"He lives upstairs in room #28. Go to the balcony. It's one of those doors there," she points east. "He's usually home in the evening."
"Hold your horses..." You hear the click of a night latch, before the lady on the other side gets caught in a coughing spasm.
"Huh," the cleaning lady says, "I thought Revachol *was* the capital."
"I already told you I don't care about any badges."
"I don't believe in equality. Never seen it work." She shakes her head and returns to sweeping.
"I don't care about your stinkin' badge. Just come in," she manages to say with a wheeze.
"I don't like talking about them," she says mostly to herself.
"I don't like talking about those people," she looks down the hallway.
"I don't want to talk about de Ruyters," the cleaning lady mutters. She starts digging for something in her pockets.
"I know my rights! And don't you 'ma'am' me, boy!" the voice snaps back.
"I know those types, yes. There have been some here, but they never make their rent. So they have to move out. I know their type..." She coughs.
"I see..." She takes out her handkerchief and wipes her nose. "I hope some good people are finally going to move in. This place needs them."
"I think he studies astrology at the community college. Education's good, I always tell them to study."
"I'd wager you've got the wrong man. But even so, you're out of luck, policeman -- I saw him leave the building just before you came in."
"I'm fine, fine, don't you worry about me!" She starts coughing, red spots appearing on her cheeks.
"I'm no one, just an old woman who cleans these hallways."
"If it ain't my business I keep my nose out of it..." She shakes her head and mutters to herself.
"If you can call it living..." She spits on the floor, before wiping it off with a broom. "I have a little room upstairs, right next to the coal room."
"Impossible," the cleaning lady says, shaking her head, "I would know if someone had moved in there." She pauses, eyeing the hallway.
"It doesn't matter who I am. Now go on, get out of here!"
"It's about Victor, isn't it?" She narrows her pale grey eyes. "It's always about Victor with her... You'll find the Méjeans in apartment #20 upstairs. It's one of the doors on the balcony."
"It's barely bigger than a closet, but I don't complain, no..." She juts out her chin, eyes shining. "I have my bed and my aching bones to keep me company and that's all I need from this world."
"Maybe it's those *counterculture people* again? Breaking into our house like it's a public space... You're a policeman, be good and take a look, will you?"
"Murder!" The cleaning lady starts laughing, but it turns into a violent coughing spasm. She squeezes her broom, trying to catch her breath.
"Never heard of it," the cleaning lady replies, before another coughing spell takes hold of her.
"No one likes them in this building." She shakes her head. "It's only because of the kid they haven't been thrown out."
"No one lives there, it's been empty for months."
"No, I already told you, I won't be responsible for any more strangers getting into the building..."
"Now, what do you want from me, policeman?"
"Oh, I do like wizards," she agrees wholeheartedly. "And people like that in general. They have a lot to tell us about our fates..."
"Oh, that one is a scientist, a future scholar!" Suddenly the old lady's face is beaming.
"Oh, you'll find plenty of Martins here, don't you worry!" She smiles a gap toothed smile when she hears you mention the name.
"Pea-brain, someone played a trick on you. Martin Martinaise is a name for *anyone* from Martinaise. Like Jim Jamrock or Raoul Revachol."
"People come and go, I don't keep an eye on everyone."
"She leaves an old lady to her business. More than I can say for others..."
"Some lunatic lost his mind... All kinds of morons pass through these halls."
"Something to do with all those stars around his door. He asked me to leave his drawings up on the wall."
"Stop banging on the door! I'm not letting any more strangers inside."
"Suit yourself, Mr. Important. No one cares about this building any way..."
"Talk!" The cleaning lady starts laughing, but it turns into a violent coughing spasm. She squeezes her broom, trying to catch her breath.
"That's what I said, astrology."
"The *artist*?" She scoffs. "Nothing I can do about her, I'm afraid. She ruins the walls faster than I can clean them. Still..." She leans on her broom.
"The cold never does any good for my bronchitis..." She sneezes into a dirty handkerchief.
"The de Ruyters..." She frowns. "He's chained it and fallen into a stupor again."
"The hell am I supposed to know?" The cleaning lady shrugs, her mouth puckered like a dried fig. "Another nut job, I assume."
"The less said about those people, the better."
"The police?! Everyone knows the police don't come around *here*.“ The hallways echoes with her cackle.
"The symbol of what now?"
"They don't like me cleaning behind their door, think I'm listening in on their fights."
"Think we'd all be better off if people kept their noses to themselves."
"What's he in trouble for?"
"What?" She frowns. "No. Nobody tells me anything."
"Yes, well..." She doesn't know what to say so she just coughs and repeats: "I hope they're good people."
"Yes-yes. I know who you mean. The scrawny boy who's always smoking like the devil, right?" She looks at the other end of the hallway.
"You don't scare me, punk! I may be an old woman but I can still take the likes of you!"
